rationale: The closest tea consumption studies have no verified brewed-tea comparison against olfactory scores. Two Parkinson studies record tea and hyposmia separately, with their joint analysis and preparation unverified. Smell tests that present tea as an odor measure a different exposure. The clinical direction remains open.

The Parkinson corn-oil comparison favored DHA plus EPA on depression response while the comparator also had responders. The authentic table and oil grade remain open. In non-Parkinson studies, both the coronary mixed-oil trial and the Alzheimer OmegAD full-sample depression comparison were inconclusive. None isolates refined corn oil against no oil.

Corn-oil comparator studies use different populations, combined treatments and broader sleep metrics. The Alzheimer OmegAD nighttime behavior item gave an inconclusive contrast and changing item-positive counts. A rated Parkinson insomnia comparison with identified refined corn oil remains unresolved.

A brewed lemongrass study measured recalled dreams and nightmares outside Parkinson disease. Aroma and topical studies report or plan global sleep or combined distressing dream measures. The new mixed topical registration has no posted results. Witnessed dream enactment or REM without atonia after brewed lemongrass remains unverified.
